2026-12-15.weatherAlert: Tokyo in mid-December can be brisk and clear, but occasional rain is possible. If raining on arrival, the Omoide Yokocho outdoor stalls will be cramped and smoky under umbrellas.
tips: Hit the Limousine Bus ATM or convenience store ATM to withdraw JPY; with the current ~161 JPY/USD rate, you'll get great value.
Use the MSP layover to add Suica to your Apple/Google Wallet so you're ready to tap-and-go the second you land.

2026-12-16.weatherAlert: High rain risk for an outdoor-heavy day. Meiji Shrine walk and Shibuya Blue Cave outdoor illumination are exposed.

suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Miyashita Park covered rooftop + Parco + Tower Records
suggestedSwap.reason: If it rains, the 600k outdoor LED walk along Yoyogi Park will be miserable; the covered Miyashita Park and Parco complex keeps you dry and entertained.

tips: Shibuya Sky sunset slots sell out fast; if you haven't pre-booked, pivot to Mag's Park rooftop or Hikarie 11F Sky Lobby.
Pre-download offline maps for Tokyo; cell service can be spotty in underground arcades.

2026-12-17.weatherAlert: Senso-ji and Nakamise are mostly outdoors/covered walkways; rain makes the market cramped but manageable.
tips: Arrive at Senso-ji right at 08:30 to beat the tour buses for clear photos of the incense burner.
If the Skytree queue is insane, pivot to the Asahi Beer Hall 22F Sky Room next door for the same river view with a drink in hand.
teamLab Planets is barefoot and involves wading through water; December floors are cold, so wear warm socks you don't mind getting slightly damp.
Golden Gai bars seat 6-8 people max; split the squad and share findings via group chat.

2026-12-19.weatherAlert: Coastal Kamakura and Enoshima are highly exposed to winter winds and rain. The Enoden tram ride and Fuji view require clear skies.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Enoshima island — climb to the Sea Candle
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Enoshima onsen finish: Enospa overlooks the bay
suggestedSwap.reason: If it's raining or bitterly cold with high winds, climbing the exposed Enoshima island will be miserable; Enospa offers a warm soak with the same bay view.

tips: December is peak clarity for Mt. Fuji—if the sky is clear, the sunset view over Sagami Bay will be epic; if cloudy, skip the Sea Candle.
Grab a hot corn soup or canned coffee from a platform vending machine to stay warm on the train.
If you didn't secure Ghibli Museum tickets, pivot to Nakano Broadway for an incredible otaku deep-dive without the entry fee.
Run the Airbnb washer during dinner so everyone lands in Kyoto with a clean kit.

2026-12-21.weatherAlert: Gion's golden hour and Shirakawa canal walk are less magical in heavy rain.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Gion at golden hour — Hanamikoji + Shirakawa canal
suggestedSwap.reason: If it's pouring, walking the exposed canal and streets loses its charm; the Manga Museum is an indoor, massive time-vortex that keeps the whole group dry.

tips: Grab ekiben at Tokyo Station before boarding—there are 200+ kinds and it's a ritual.
Sit on the LEFT side of the Nozomi (Seat E) for the Mt. Fuji view around minute 40.

2026-12-22.weatherAlert: Fushimi Inari at dawn is slippery when wet; the stone steps become hazardous in rain.

suggestedSwap.reason: If it's raining heavily, the thousands of wet, uneven stone steps at Fushimi Inari are a slip hazard; Sanjusangendo offers a jaw-dropping, entirely indoor alternative.

tips: Vending machine hot corn soup on the descent is a winter lifesaver—don't skip it.
Funaoka Onsen has a 1923 'electric bath'—it's weirdly tingly and a quintessential sento experience.

2026-12-23.weatherAlert: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is highly exposed; rain makes the path extremely crowded with umbrellas and ruins photos.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove before the buses exist
suggestedSwap.reason: If it rains, the narrow Arashiyama path becomes an umbrella traffic jam; Hokokuji offers a quieter, partially covered bamboo grove with matcha indoors.

tips: Wakakusa-yama is closed for the winter (closes 2nd Sunday of December), so don't attempt the climb.
Bow to the deer with empty hands to show you're out of crackers—they actually understand this gesture!
KFC for Christmas dinner is no joke in Japan—pre-order or expect to wait in a massive line.
If you lost the Nintendo Museum lottery, Uji's Byodo-in and matcha scene easily fills the morning.

2026-12-25.crowdAlert: USJ on Christmas Day will be at peak capacity, especially for Super Nintendo World.
tips: Rope-drop 45 minutes early and head STRAIGHT to Super Nintendo World; timed entry fills up instantly.
If Express Passes are sold out, use single-rider lines to cut 60% off Mario Kart wait times.

2026-12-26.weatherAlert: Miyajima's floating torii is best at low tide, but rain makes the ferry ride and island walk cold and windy.
tips: This is the longest day of the trip; if anyone is redlining, it's okay to skip Miyajima and wait at Hiroshima Station.
The Peace Memorial Museum hits heavy—that's the point. Shukkei-en garden nearby offers a quiet, reflective space to decompress.

2026-12-27.weatherAlert: Midosuji Illumination is a 4km outdoor walk; cold, rainy winter weather can make this miserable.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: MIDOSUJI ILLUMINATION — 4km of lit boulevard, walked south
suggestedSwap.reason: If it's pouring and freezing, a 4km outdoor walk loses its appeal; the indoor Osaka Museum of Housing & Living offers a life-size Edo street experience out of the cold.

tips: Buy 551 Horai pork buns at Namba station BEFORE the crab dinner—they sell out nightly and make the best next-day breakfast.
Split squads for the afternoon: nerds hit Den Den Town, hypebeasts hit Amerikamura.
Kobe beef lunch sets are significantly cheaper than dinner; save the splurge for midday.
Do a tax-free paperwork check tonight: ensure receipts are with passports and purchases are accessible for customs on exit.
Sit on the LEFT side (Seat A) of the Nozomi heading east for one last Mt. Fuji view.
Zero out your Suica balance at the konbini or station machine before flying; refunds are a hassle at the airport.

globalTips: With the USD/JPY rate hovering around 161, your dollar stretches far—withdraw larger sums at 7-Eleven ATMs to minimize per-transaction fees and pay in JPY (not USD) if credit cards prompt you to choose.
December in Japan is cold, dry, and occasionally rainy; pack versatile layers, a solid rain shell, and comfortable, slip-resistant walking shoes for wet temple steps.
Pre-book major attractions (teamLab, USJ Express Pass, Shibuya Sky) as far in advance as possible—December crowds are real, and walk-up tickets are rarely available.
